TestTopology::test_crash_during_decommis.description: 3-node cluster (RBNO forced for bootstrap/decommission, small-table RBNO off), decommission node1 in a background thread while hard-killing/restarting node2 (up to 10 times; after the 10th waits for node3 to see node2 DN before restarting). Joins the thread (bounded, asserted dead), then polls node2's raw `nodetool status` (120s, 300s debug): node1 absent if the decommission succeeded else UN, node2/node3 present, every row UN (a '?' status row fails). Ported from Cassandra CASSANDRA-10231 (invalid entries for the decommissioned node after a crash); in practice the kill makes the raft decommission fail and roll back.

origin.summary: Cassandra dtest reproducing CASSANDRA-10231; enabled for scylla in fcc77da925 (PR #387). PR #52 in data is the upstream merge.

TestTopology::test_crash_during_decommis.reason: Can't-fail ' null ' assert fixed by 3c3a95dc9a (PR #7512): now a polled convergence check on node2's raw nodetool status that catches '?' rows and a lingering/non-UN node1. Partial overlap only: test_kill_coordinator_during_decommission (kill during decommission -> rollback -> restart -> consistency, injection, release-skipped) and test_topology_streaming_failure (rollback); dtest uniquely kills a bystander repeatedly in release mode. Note: decommission practically always fails after the kill, so the succeeded/node1-absent branch (the CASSANDRA-10231 scenario) is ~never exercised. Note: ' null ' early-break in the kill loop is still dead (topology_test.py:115). 100% pass, ~77s.
